Lessons.Title: Division With and Without Remainders
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will use an algorithm that uses partial quotients to find whole number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors.
In this lesson, you deepen and apply what you learned about partial quotients to divide four-digit numbers by single-digit divisors.

Source activity sequence: Warm-up: Notice and Wonder: Equations with Hundreds (10 minutes); Activity 1: A Stack of Partial Quotients (15 minutes); Activity 2: Andre and Elena’s Work (10 minutes); Activity 3: Incomplete Calculations (10 minutes); Cool-down: Find a Quotient (5 minutes)
Exact mathematical focus: A whole-number division result must satisfy dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder, with remainder smaller than divisor.
Edulytics authored model: 389 − (7 × 50) = 39. 39 − (7 × 5) = 4. 389 = 7 × 55 + 4; the remainder 4 is less than 7.
First-party Cool-down: Find 947 ÷ 4 and give the quotient and remainder.
Original diagrams, live construction, classroom response, and publisher login-gated Cool-down are not digitally certified.
